scope: Corollary 4.4 (Depth-zero normalization and vanishing-depth nodes) of the manuscript “Every four-dimensional Kakeya set has full Hausdorff dimension” (preprints/Every-four-dimensional-Kakeya-set-has-full-Hausdorff-dimension-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 074 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 30d0c186aa9c697d), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 50-51. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: A sequence of depth-zero, horizon-zero known normalizations of a maximizing sequence is again maximizing, provided the 50 normalizations have the actual subpower success and terminal knowledge required in Lemma 2.13. This assertion does not require bounded absolute density exponents. On any maximizing sequence one may choose true nodes at positive depths bi → 0 whose horizon exponents tend to zero, retaining the relative-profile estimates at those nodes in the slowly diagonalized sense.
